description: IBNET, the International Benchmarking Network for Water and Sanitation Utilities, is the World Bank's database of utility performance data, relaunched as New IBNET, which describes itself as the world's largest database of its kind. It reports 2,792 utilities in 152 countries. Utilities and regulators share data on 15 harmonised key performance indicators and answer a 27-question self-assessment of management practices in seven categories, and users can compare a utility with a region and explore water tariffs worldwide; the site also carries news, events and case stories from utilities such as Sofia Water and Quito's EPMAPS. The World Bank runs it, and utilities contribute through sign-up. Format and access: web dashboards and a data requirements document; contributing and some services need registration. Licence: not stated, with an all rights reserved notice; free to use. Caveats: data are self-reported and coverage varies by year and country, and the bulk export route was not found on the home page. It gives service performance baselines for capacity planning and resilience models of water utilities. Related catalogue records are Mexico's PIGOO indicators and India's Performance Assessment System, national benchmarking schemes.
